nodes.label: PERMISSION_DEFS
nodes.rationale: The single source in src/lib/server/permissions.ts. Permissions are developer-defined at build time and an admin never creates or edits one, so a new module or action is added there and nowhere else.

nodes.label: PERMISSIONS
nodes.rationale: Records submodule at build time while the parts were still separate, which is why a key's submodule is looked up rather than computed. UI grouping reads this in TypeScript, not the permission table row and not the key string.

nodes.label: PERMISSION_IMPLIES
nodes.rationale: Stores single steps only and must never be read directly.

nodes.label: expandPermissions
nodes.rationale: Walks the implication chain all the way up and is idempotent, so it is safe to apply anywhere. Unrecognised keys pass through untouched rather than being dropped, so a leftover database row never silently removes access it was already granting.

nodes.label: Super-admin role
nodes.rationale: Identified by a live condition — does the role hold admin:manage_roles, read from role_permission — rather than an is_protected column. Frozen: only description is editable; name, status and permission set are locked; deletion, deactivation and duplication are blocked. Exactly one holder role, never zero active users, and it can only be granted by someone who already holds it or by the bootstrap script.

nodes.label: Role editor
nodes.rationale: Asks which kind of role up front and then shows only that key set. Saves exactly what was ticked, since auto-tick already includes every implied key, but still runs expandPermissions server-side because a POST can be crafted in the browser.

nodes.label: Admin role
nodes.rationale: Holds only admin:* keys and works inside /admin/*. A staff permission is unusable to an admin user because their navigation shows only admin pages and the hooks.server.ts guard blocks a typed staff URL, so the two kinds are never mixed in one role.

nodes.label: Staff role
nodes.rationale: Holds only non-admin keys and works inside the staff routes. Admin data pages mirror the staff ones as separate routes rather than one route branching on permissions, because the admin table has features the staff table does not.

nodes.label: create-admin.ts bootstrap
nodes.rationale: Runs on the production server after build via tsx, reading source rather than build output. Finds the super-admin role by permission, never by name, because a role name is runtime data an admin can rename.

nodes.label: sync-permissions.ts
nodes.rationale: Permission rows are data, not schema, so drizzle-kit generate produces nothing for a new key and this script must be run after any PERMISSION_DEFS change. Orphan deletion is always offered and never skipped, because 'missing from the code' could mean removed for good or absent from the checked-out branch and the script cannot tell them apart, while which roles held a key is recorded nowhere but the database. Grants are deleted before permission rows because role_permission.permission_fk has no onDelete and MySQL restricts.

nodes.label: Role templates
nodes.rationale: Pre-checked defaults only, never saved as records of their own. The Admin template is derived by filtering the Roles keys out rather than listing keys by hand, so a new admin page is picked up automatically while the Roles page stays excluded.

nodes.label: Permission key shape
nodes.rationale: Keys are built forward and never split back apart: '_' is both the separator and a legal character inside a submodule name, so admin:view_org_units reads equally well as view + org_units or view_org + units and nothing in the string resolves it. One level of submodules only, every module must define view because that is the key each route's load checks, plural for countable things, and data modules appear twice on purpose.

nodes.label: Roles page restriction
nodes.rationale: Both Roles keys are absent from the role editor rather than greyed out, so no admin can violate the one-holder rule through the UI and the holder check exists only as a safety net. admin:view_roles is withheld alongside admin:manage_roles because a Roles page nobody can edit has no reason to exist, so its read-only rendering is never built — the one admin page that does not follow the view/manage split.

nodes.label: src/lib/rbac/access.ts helpers
nodes.rationale: Every access check tests a permission key, never a role name, because role names are runtime data an admin can rename while keys are defined in source and cannot change underneath the code.

nodes.label: hooks.server.ts route guard
nodes.rationale: The normal permission guard already blocks an admin user typing a staff URL, so nothing special is needed to keep the two kinds of role apart at the route level.

nodes.label: Role editor auto-tick rule
nodes.rationale: Ticking any non-view action ticks that module's view, because managing a page you cannot open is meaningless; unticking view clears every other action in the module. This is what makes the stored ticked set already closed under implication.

nodes.label: Fuel approve permission key (still open)
nodes.rationale: Fuel is the only module with an approval step, so it is the only one needing an approve key: a staff member requests a withdrawal slip, GSU approves it physically with a signature, and the key controls who may afterwards mark it approved. Electricity, water, paper, ESWM and GHG record data without approval. Exact key list undecided.

nodes.label: No user changes their own role
nodes.rationale: Prevents self-promotion and also self-lockout, where an admin strips their own admin:manage_users and loses the only page that could undo it. Together with 'only a super-admin assigns super-admin' it closes the grant path completely in both directions.

hyperedges.label: The mechanisms that keep exactly one unweakenable super-admin role
